title: Dithiol Glutaredoxin 1 Overexpression in Leishmania donovani Regulates Thiol Homeostasis to Enhance Oxidative Stress Tolerance and Parasite Survival
content: Rise of co-infected cases, drug-resistance, asymptomatic infections, and limited treatment options increases difficulties to treat VL infections, which challenges VL elimination. Thiol redox metabolism plays crucial role in parasite survival, and emerged as a promising drug target. In trypanosomatids, glutaredoxins are low molecular weight oxidoreductases that play a crucial role in preserving redox homeostasis. The present study aims to investigate the roles of Grx1 protein of Leishmania donovani in parasite survival, drug resistance, oxidative stress tolerance, and infectivity. LdGrx1 overexpression in L. donovani exhibited increased enzymatic activity, parasite proliferation, and survivability than control parasites. The Grx1-OE showed increased tolerance towards Amp-B, H2O2, and menadione, suggesting the role of Grx1 protein in defense of oxidative stress. Further, Grx1-OE parasite possessed higher intracellular thiol levels, enhanced antioxidant enzymatic activities, and decreased ROS levels, suggesting that Grx1 protein is involved in modulating Leishmania’s redox biology. Grx1-OE also showed increased expression of thiol-pathway proteins, resembling the pattern of drug-resistant-parasites, suggesting its role in sustaining redox balance. Additionally, Grx1-OE boosts parasite’s infectivity and its survival as demonstrated by the in-vitro assessment of THP1 macrophage infectivity. Therefore, our findings provide detailed understanding into how LdGrx1-mediated thiol homeostasis may contribute to parasite survival under oxidative stress.
